obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Any severity-1 incident, or any incident affecting field operations, owner or partner data, or financial reporting
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (company standard: committee convenes within 48 hours of declaration)
notify: Disclosure committee (internal determination, recorded in minutes)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
clock_starts: Date and time of the materiality determination

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies; request goes through outside counsel to the Department of Justice

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Severity-1 incident that may be material
deadline: At the first disclosure committee meeting
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay, or a fixed number of days); counsel state matrix
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - royalty owners live in all 50 states; employees in at least 9 states
clock_starts: Per each state law (often discovery or determination of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above the state-set count of affected residents
deadline: Varies by state

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above the state-set count
deadline: Varies by state

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; contracts require notice within 10 days of determination (Florida standard applied to all vendors)
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - payroll, print and mail, bank, telematics, and accounting software vendors

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security affecting Florida residents (royalty owners: names with Social Security numbers or bank account numbers with access codes; employees: Social Security, driver license, health plan, or geolocation information)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the department within 30 days; delay on written law enforcement request
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if personal information of Floridians was accessed
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to the notice to individuals)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination provided to the department within 30 days after the determination; kept at least 5 years

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: Agent must notify the company no later than 10 days after determination; the company then gives the (3) and (4) notices

obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
citation: 40 CFR 110.6; 33 CFR part 153 subpart B (Clean Water Act section 311(b)(3))
trigger: Discharge of oil in a quantity that may be harmful (for example a tank overflow or gathering line release after loss of SCADA control that reaches water)
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge has knowledge
notify: National Response Center (800-424-8802); if not practicable, the Coast Guard or EPA on-scene coordinator
owner: Vice President, Health, Safety, and Environment

obligation: PHMSA immediate notice of an accident (regulated rural gathering lines)
trigger: Release from one of the 44 regulated rural gathering miles that meets 195.52(a) (death or hospitalization, unintentional fire or explosion, property damage over $50,000, water pollution, or significant in the operator's judgment)
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, and no later than one hour after confirmed discovery
notify: National Response Center (800-424-8802), with the initial estimate of product released (195.52(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 44 regulated rural miles only; 195.15(c)(2) excludes reporting-regulated-only lines

obligation: PHMSA revised or confirmed notice
trigger: After an immediate notice
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable

obligation: PHMSA accident report
trigger: Release meeting 195.50 from any company crude gathering line (regulated rural or reporting-regulated-only)
deadline: As soon as practicable but no later than 30 days after discovery (DOT Form 7000-1); supplemental report within 30 days of changes
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all company crude gathering lines

obligation: State oil and gas regulator spill and incident reports
citation: State oil and gas commission rules (Texas, Oklahoma, and Florida operations)
trigger: Release or fire at a well, tank battery, or facility that meets the state threshold
deadline: Per each state rule; listed in the HSE state reporting matrix
owner: Vice President, Health, Safety, and Environment

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: No current legal requirement (see the CIRCIA row); CISA and FBI reporting channels
trigger: Ransomware or any intrusion that reaches the OT DMZ or SCADA
deadline: As soon as practicable; the runbook targets day 0 to 1
notify: CISA (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; supports the OFAC mitigating factor

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report and ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, the company would be covered by the size test (P03 G-133); the draft report path in section 4 is kept ready
clock_starts: Proposed: reasonable belief of a covered incident

obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-notified pipeline owner or operator
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - TSA has not notified the company (N21-R02 not applicable, P03 G-132)

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities, OCS facilities, or vessels
trigger: Cyber incident involving or endangering a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1)
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or the National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - onshore only; no vessel, waterfront facility, or OCS facility (N21-R01 not applicable, P03 G-131)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article identified in contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: SL-2 water services customer notice
trigger: Incident affecting water gathering and disposal service, volume tickets, or customer data
deadline: Per agreement (24 hours for a service outage; 72 hours for a security incident affecting customer data)

obligation: Owner and partner communications (SL-1)
citation: Joint operating agreements; owner portal terms (contract)
trigger: Incident delaying statements or payments, or affecting owner or partner data
deadline: Per agreement; portal notice before a delayed payment run

obligation: Crude purchaser, pipeline, and gas gatherer notices
citation: Crude purchase, transportation, and gas purchase agreements (contract)
trigger: Incident that stops or reduces deliveries, or affects ticket data exchanges
deadline: Per each contract (force majeure and nomination change notices)
notify: Crude purchasers; transmission pipelines; gas gathering companies

obligation: Lender and credit agreement notices
trigger: Event that could be a material adverse effect under the agreement
deadline: Per agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; CFO checks with counsel
